# Ezekiel 24 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-me in-the-ninth year, in-the-tenth month, on-the-tenth of-the-month, saying:

**2** "Son-of man, write for-yourself the-name-of the-day, this very day; the-king-of Babylon has-laid-siege against Jerusalem this-very day.

**3** And-speak a-parable to the-house-of rebellion, and-say to-them, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Set-on the-pot, set-it-on, and-also pour water into-it.

**4** Gather its-pieces into-it, every good piece — thigh and-shoulder — fill [it with] choice bones.

**5** Take the-choice-of the-flock, and-also pile-up the-bones under-it; boil-it thoroughly, also cook its-bones in-its-midst.'

**6** Therefore thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'Woe, city-of blood — the-pot whose rust [is] in-it, and-whose rust has-not-gone-out from-it! Piece by-piece bring-it-out — no lot has-fallen upon-it.

**7** For her-blood is in-her-midst; upon a-bare rock she-placed-it; she-did-not-pour-it upon the-ground to-cover-it with-dust.

**8** To-bring-up fury, to-take vengeance, I-have-placed her-blood upon a-bare rock, so-that-it-will-not-be-covered.'

**9** Therefore thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'Woe, city-of blood! I also will-make-great the-pile.

**10** Heap-on the-wood, kindle the-fire, consume the-flesh, and-pour-out the-broth, and-the-bones shall-be-charred.

**11** And-set-it upon its-coals empty, so-that it-heats and-its-copper burns, and-its-uncleanness melts in-it, its-rust is-consumed.

**12** With-toil she-has-wearied, and-her-great rust has-not-gone-out from-her; in-the-fire [goes] her-rust.

**13** In-your-uncleanness [is] lewdness; because I-cleansed-you and-you-were-not-cleansed, from-your-uncleanness you-will-not-be-cleansed again until I-have-spent My-fury upon-you.

**14** I, YHWH, have-spoken; it-comes and-I-will-do [it]; I-will-not-relent, and-I-will-not-spare, and-I-will-not-be-sorry; according-to your-ways and-according-to your-deeds they-will-judge-you,' declares the-Lord YHWH."

**15** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-me, saying:

**16** "Son-of man, behold-Me taking from-you the-desire-of your-eyes with-a-plague; but-you-shall-not-lament, and-you-shall-not-weep, and-your-tears shall-not-come.

**17** Groan silently; mourning-for [the]-dead do-not-make; your-turban bind upon-you, and-your-sandals put upon your-feet, and-do-not-cover [your]-upper-lip, and-the-bread-of men do-not-eat."

**18** And-I-spoke to the-people in-the-morning, and-my-wife died in-the-evening; and-I-did in-the-morning as I-was-commanded.

**19** And-the-people said to-me, "Will-you-not-tell us what these [things mean] to-us, that you-do [them]?"

**20** And-I-said to-them, "The-word-of YHWH came to-me, saying:

**21** 'Say to-the-house-of Israel: Thus says the-Lord YHWH: Behold-Me profaning My-sanctuary — the-pride-of your-strength, the-desire-of your-eyes, and-the-yearning-of your-soul; and-your-sons and-your-daughters whom you-left behind — by-the-sword they-shall-fall.

**22** And-you-shall-do as I-have-done: the-upper-lip you-shall-not-cover, and-the-bread-of men you-shall-not-eat.

**23** And-your-turbans [shall be] upon your-heads and-your-sandals upon your-feet; you-shall-not-lament and-you-shall-not-weep, but-you-shall-rot in-your-iniquities and-groan, each to-his-brother.

**24** And-Ezekiel shall-be to-you for-a-sign; according-to all which he-did, you-shall-do. When-it-comes, then-you-shall-know that I [am] the-Lord YHWH.'

**25** And-you, son-of man — is-it-not on-the-day I-take from-them their-stronghold, the-joy-of their-beauty, the-desire-of their-eyes and-the-yearning-of their-soul — their-sons and-their-daughters —

**26** on-that day the-one-who-escapes shall-come to-you, to-cause [your]-ears to-hear?

**27** On-that day your-mouth shall-be-opened to the-one-who-escapes, and-you-shall-speak and-be-mute no-longer; and-you-shall-be to-them for-a-sign, and-they-shall-know that I [am] YHWH."

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **24:2**: The exact date — the tenth of Tevet, 588 BCE — when the siege of Jerusalem began. This date becomes a fast day in Jewish tradition (Asarah be-Tevet). Ezekiel, in Babylon, records the event in real time.

- **24:16-18**: Machmad einekha — 'the desire of your eyes.' God takes Ezekiel's wife as a prophetic sign. The prohibition against mourning parallels what Israel must do when the Temple falls — the loss too great for normal grief.

- **24:27**: Yippatach pikha — 'your mouth shall be opened.' Ezekiel's enforced silence (since 3:26) will end when Jerusalem falls. The prophetic voice returns only when the judgment it predicted arrives.

— EMET
